R005.definition: scrolls (plural of megillah); the five Megillot are short books read at Jewish festivals: Song of Songs (Passover), Ruth (Shavuot), Lamentations (Tisha B'Av), Ecclesiastes (Sukkot), Esther (Purim).

R006.definition: Writings; the third division of the Hebrew Bible (Tanakh), after Torah and Nevi'im (Prophets). Includes Psalms, Proverbs, Job, the five Megillot, Daniel, Ezra-Nehemiah, and Chronicles.

R007.definition: counting (construct form); as in Sefirat HaOmer, the 49-day count from Passover to Shavuot (Leviticus 23:15-16). Ruth's story spans this period.

R008.definition: the omer; a measure of grain (~2.3 liters) and the first sheaf offering waved before the Lord at Passover (Leviticus 23:10-14), beginning the count to Shavuot.

R009.definition: a Moabite woman (feminine gentilic); the halachic distinction Mo'avi v'lo Mo'avit — 'a Moabite man is forbidden, but not a Moabite woman' — permitted Ruth's inclusion (Yevamot 76b).

R010.definition: unnamed, anonymous; used with peloni to mean 'so-and-so.' The anonymous kinsman in Ruth 4 is called peloni almoni — his name erased because he refused to redeem.

R011.definition: widespread, spread abroad (niphal participle of parats, H6555); in 1 Samuel 3:1 — 'there was no vision nifrats (widespread)' — prophecy existed but was not spreading.

R013.definition: from (the) father; the folk etymology of Moab (Mo'av) — parsed as me-av, 'from father,' referencing Lot's incestuous origin story (Genesis 19:37).

G1656f1.definition: mercy, compassion, pity; the LXX's most common rendering of Hebrew chesed, though it loses the covenant-loyalty dimension.

G202f1.definition: nearest kinsman, one with right of redemption; the LXX term for Hebrew go'el in Ruth — the legal kinsman-redeemer.

G3086f1.definition: redeemer, deliverer; from lytron (ransom). Used in Acts 7:35 for Moses as deliverer; the broader LXX equivalent of go'el.

G3813f1.definition: a young boy, little child; diminutive of pais (child/servant). The LXX term for Hebrew na'ar when referring to the young Samuel.

G3816f1.definition: a child, boy, youth; also servant, attendant. Covers both dimensions of Hebrew na'ar — age and service status.

G11f1.definition: Ebenezer (transliterated from Hebrew Even ha-Ezer); the memorial stone Samuel set up after Israel's victory: 'Hitherto hath the LORD helped us' (1 Samuel 7:12).

G3037f1.definition: a stone; used broadly in LXX and NT. Christ is called 'the stone which the builders rejected' (Psalm 118:22; Matthew 21:42).

G996f1.definition: help, aid, assistance; the Greek equivalent of Hebrew ezer. Used in Hebrews 4:16 — 'find grace to help in time of need.'

G191f1.definition: to hear, listen, understand; root of English 'acoustic.' The Greek equivalent of Hebrew shama — though Greek separates hearing from obeying, while Hebrew unites them.

G5219f1.definition: to obey (literally 'to hear under,' i.e., to submit to what is heard); the Greek word that captures Hebrew shama's hearing-obeying unity. Root of English 'obey' (via Latin oboedire, 'to hear toward').
